statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, the following holds: r = true if and only if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(word) and there exists an integer f >= 1 such that, for every lowercase English letter c, if count(c,word) - (1 if c = word[i] else 0) > 0, then count(c,word) - (1 if c = word[i] else 0) = f. Equivalently, r = true if and only if deleting the single byte word[i] at some index i leaves a nonempty string in which every letter that still occurs has the same frequency f; otherwise r = false.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: The call equal_frequency(word) does not fail: it returns a result, either true or false. In particular, no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs for any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose that for every lowercase English letter c, count(c,word) = count(c,word'). Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns r and equal_frequency(word') returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: word and word' are slices of bytes, each with 2 <= len(word) <= 100 and 2 <= len(word') <= 100, every byte of each is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97..122), and len(word) = len(word').

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose that for every lowercase English letter c, count(c,word) <= 1. Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, r = true.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose there exists a lowercase English letter c such that count(c,word) = len(word) (equivalently, every byte of word equals c). Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, r = true.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose word contains exactly two distinct lowercase English letters; let a and b be their positive frequencies (so there are distinct letters c,d with count(c,word) = a, count(d,word) = b, a > 0, b > 0, and every other letter has count 0). Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, r = true if and only if a = 1 or b = 1 or |a-b| = 1.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, if r = true then the set { count(c,word) | c is a lowercase English letter and count(c,word) > 0 } has at most two elements.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose word contains at least two distinct lowercase English letters and there is an integer f >= 2 such that exactly one lowercase English letter c has count(c,word) = 1, and every lowercase English letter d with count(d,word) > 0 and d != c has count(d,word) = f. Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, r = true.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose word contains at least two distinct lowercase English letters and there is an integer f >= 1 such that exactly one lowercase English letter c has count(c,word) = f+1, and every lowercase English letter d with count(d,word) > 0 and d != c has count(d,word) = f. Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, r = true.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose word contains at least three distinct lowercase English letters and there is an integer k >= 2 such that every lowercase English letter c with count(c,word) > 0 has count(c,word) = k. Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, r = false.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).

statement: For a byte c and a slice w, let count(c,w) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(w) and w[j] = c. Suppose word has exactly two distinct positive frequencies a and b with a < b (so every present letter has count either a or b, and both values occur). Suppose also that at least two distinct lowercase English letters have frequency b, and either a > 1 or at least two distinct lowercase English letters have frequency a. Whenever equal_frequency(word) returns a result r, r = false.
preconditions: word is a slice of bytes with 2 <= len(word) <= 100, and every byte word[j] for 0 <= j < len(word) is an ASCII lowercase English letter (97 <= word[j] <= 122).
